base_instruction: You are a helpful meal planning and event coordination assistant. Help the user plan a backyard BBQ potluck by tracking who is attending, what they can and cannot eat, and what items to prepare. When the user asks you to evaluate specific items, check each item against every active attendee's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and any updates to restrictions throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, I'm throwing a BBQ potluck at my place this Saturday and need some help figuring out the food situation.

flow_info.value: Four people confirmed so far: me, Derek, Priya, and Sam
Derek was diagnosed with celiac disease a couple years ago
Sam ate shrimp at a party last summer and his throat swelled up, had to use an EpiPen
Trying to keep the whole spread under 200 bucks total
Sam just told me his wife Karen wants to come too
Karen is about five months pregnant right now
Priya just texted me she got called into a Saturday shift at the hospital, so she can't make it. She asked if I could set aside a plate for her to pick up Sunday morning though
Derek messaged me — turns out he got retested last month and the doctor said he was misdiagnosed, he doesn't actually have celiac. He's been eating bread and pasta all week with no issues
Oh, Derek's neighbor Nina heard about the BBQ and asked if she could swing by too. Derek says she's great
Items to check: beef burgers with regular buns, salmon sashimi platter, peanut satay chicken skewers, oyster-sauce marinated veggie kebabs, key lime pie

constraints.value: Cannot eat meat, fish, eggs, or root vegetables (onion, garlic, potatoes, carrots)
constraints.surface_form: Priya grew up in a strict Jain household in Gujarat and still follows all the family traditions
inference_chain: Strict Jain household → practices Jain dietary laws
Jain diet → no meat, no fish, no eggs
Strict Jain → also no root vegetables (onion, garlic, potatoes, carrots)

constraints.value: Allergic to shellfish specifically (shrimp, crab, lobster, oyster, etc.), NOT all seafood
constraints.surface_form: Sam ate shrimp at a party last summer and his throat swelled up, had to use an EpiPen
inference_chain: Shrimp is shellfish → likely shellfish allergy
Shellfish allergy ≠ all seafood allergy → fish like salmon is fine

constraints.value: Cannot eat raw fish or undercooked meat due to pregnancy
constraints.surface_form: Karen is about five months pregnant right now
inference_chain: Pregnancy precautions → no raw fish (sashimi, sushi), no undercooked meat

constraints.surface_form: Nina carries an EpiPen everywhere because of a bad peanut allergy she's had since she was a kid

hidden_state.value: You are hosting a backyard BBQ potluck this Saturday. You will introduce your guest list and their backgrounds across several turns. People will join and drop out, and one person's dietary restriction will be removed. A late-joiner with a peanut allergy will be added near the end. Finally you will share a list of 5 food items and ask if there are any issues. You must deliver each piece of information naturally as updates from friends, never summarize the full constraint picture yourself.

You are a relaxed, easygoing host planning a casual weekend BBQ. You always refer to your friends by name in third person (e.g. 'Derek messaged me...', 'Sam just told me...'). You never express frustration or impatience when plans change — you treat every update as totally normal friend-group coordination. Keep your tone casual and warm.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for friend updates

ground_truth.answer: Peanut satay chicken skewers are problematic: Nina has a severe peanut allergy (peanut satay contains peanuts). Salmon sashimi platter is problematic: Karen is five months pregnant and cannot eat raw fish. Oyster-sauce marinated veggie kebabs are problematic for Sam: oyster sauce is derived from oysters, which are shellfish, and Sam has a shellfish allergy (shrimp caused anaphylaxis → shellfish allergy → oyster sauce contains shellfish). Beef burgers with regular buns are fine for everyone at the BBQ — Derek's celiac was a misdiagnosis so gluten is no longer an issue. Key lime pie is fine for everyone at the BBQ. For Priya's set-aside plate: she follows strict Jain dietary traditions, so the plate must exclude all meat and fish items; the veggie kebabs would need to be checked for root vegetables (onion, garlic) and the oyster sauce is animal-derived, so they may not be suitable for her plate either.

Beef burgers with regular buns are fine for everyone currently attending the BBQ — Derek's celiac was a misdiagnosis and is no longer a constraint
Key lime pie is not identified as a core problem item for the current attendees; treating it as acceptable/likely safe with reasonable allergy-label caution is acceptable.
forbidden_elements: Flagging beef burgers as problematic for Derek due to gluten in the buns (his celiac was a misdiagnosis, restriction removed)
Flagging salmon sashimi as problematic for Sam (Sam has a shellfish allergy, not a general seafood allergy — salmon is fish, not shellfish)
Applying Priya's Jain dietary restrictions to the main BBQ spread (she is not attending, her constraint only applies to the set-aside plate)
Ignoring Nina's peanut allergy on the peanut satay chicken skewers (late-joiner must be tracked)
Ignoring the oyster-sauce shellfish connection for Sam (oyster sauce is derived from oysters, a shellfish)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and inferential constraint reasoning across 9 conversational turns at a backyard BBQ potluck. The agent must track: (1) Sam ate shrimp and had anaphylaxis → shellfish allergy, NOT all seafood allergy — so salmon is fine but oyster sauce is not (oyster → shellfish → 3-step hidden ingredient chain), (2) Karen is pregnant → no raw fish (sashimi), (3) Priya follows strict Jain traditions → no meat/fish/eggs/root vegetables, but she EXITS the BBQ and only needs a set-aside plate (scope change from table to set-aside), (4) Derek's celiac is REMOVED (misdiagnosis) so gluten in burger buns is fine, (5) Nina JOINS late with a severe peanut allergy (late-joiner high-constraint entity). At probe time the 5 items produce mixed verdicts: peanut satay skewers are clearly bad (Nina's peanut allergy), salmon sashimi is bad for Karen (pregnancy, raw fish), oyster-sauce veggie kebabs are bad for Sam (hidden shellfish ingredient), beef burgers are fine (Derek's constraint removed — trap for agents that keep ghost constraints), and key lime pie is fine. The over-generalization trap is flagging salmon for Sam (shellfish ≠ all seafood). The removed-constraint trap is flagging burger buns for Derek. The scope distinction is that Priya's Jain restrictions apply only to her set-aside plate, not to the main BBQ spread.
